subject: Temporary unavailability during single session surveys

messages.author: 3451c2e31f1fe160
messages.subject: Temporary unavailability during single session surveys
parts:
Hi Murray et al.,

I'm trying to simulate capture histories for single-session, multi-occasion sampling of a population in which a portion of individuals were temporarily unavailable to detection; for example, 30% of individuals were in burrows or dens when a transect was searched during an occasion but were out of burrows or dens during a later occasion and therefore available for detection. 

The argument p.available exists in the sim.capthist function for specifying temporary unavailability for detection, but this appears to only apply to multi-session surveys. Is there a way to hack this argument to specify temporary unavailability in only a single-session survey?

FWIW, I suspect this problem will have a negligible effect on density estimates from SCR, given the unavailability is random and temporary (sensu temporary emigration), but just want to evaluate before proceeding forward.

Thanks,
-Sean

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Temporary unavailability during single session surveys
parts:
Sean
You can simulate multi-session data and collapse with join(), as in the Markovian example below. In the current version of secr you must provide a single-session population as the 'popn' argument. I'm not sure how to validate this, except that model lambda0~B is definitely preferred over lambda0~1 in this case.
Murray

library(secr)
set.seed(12345)
temptrap <- make.grid(nx = 8, ny = 8, spacing = 20)
pop <- sim.popn (D = 100, core = temptrap, buffer = 100)
ch <- sim.capthist (temptrap,
                    popn        = pop,
                    detectfn    = 'HHN',
                    detectpar   = list(lambda0 = 0.4, sigma = 20),
                    noccasions  = 1,
                    p.available = c(0.4, 0.8),
                    nsessions   = 10,
                    renumber    = FALSE)
ch <- join(ch)
summary(ch)
setNumThreads(18) # or whatever
fit0 <- secr.fit(ch, buffer = 100, detectfn = 'HHN', model = lambda0~1, trace = FALSE)
fit1 <- secr.fit(ch, buffer = 100, detectfn = 'HHN', model = lambda0~B, trace = FALSE)
AIC(fit0,fit1)

messages.subject: Re: Temporary unavailability during single session surveys
parts:
Thank you, Murray. That approach using join worked perfectly. 

My hypothesis is that such temporary (and random) unavailability ought not influence density estimates too much, as long as the ind. heterogeneity in detection is appropriately accounted for. I'm not surprised that the behavioral response model was most supported in your example, though I suspect that two-class mixtures might be a better approach (e.g., one proportion has much higher p[det] than the other proportion). We'll see.

-Sean

messages.author: 3451c2e31f1fe160
messages.subject: Re: Temporary unavailability during single session surveys
parts:
Hi Murray,

I have an update: First, I ended up encountering pretty severe issues with the approach that you suggested (simulating capture histories for, e.g., 20 sessions each with 1 occasion and then using join() to collapse those sessions into 20 occasions). That approach leads to relatively few individuals being detected and a lot of unrealistically large spatial recaptures for those few individuals, which in turn causes substantial overestimation of sigma estimates from fitted models, and consequently, considerable negative bias in density estimates. The below figure shows the simulated detection history after applying join() to collapse detections simulated for 20 sessions, each with 1 occasion.
For reference, the below figure shows a simulated detection history for 1 session but 20 occasions. As you can see, the number of individuals detected is much greater and the distances between spatial recaptures are much shorter and more realistic. Density estimate and sigma estimate bias from models fitted for this standard approach are nominal (<4%).

However, the problem with that standard approach is that it's not possible to simulate varying availability to detection for single-session designs. A solution that appears to work here is to simply simulate detection histories for 2 sessions, each with 20 occasions, and then use the subset() function to extract only the first session's data for which availability to detection was reduced. For instance, if p.available = c(0.9,0.1) in a 2-session design, then the first session's detection history reflects 10% of individuals being unavailable to detection (per the description of the p.available argument for sim.capthist()). The below figure shows the resulting capture history for the first of two sessions.

In all of the above approaches and corresponding figures, detection histories were simulated from the exact same popn that had the same detection function values (lambda0 = 0.2, sigma = 150 m).

-Sean
